title: Tijeras Man Indicted for Attempting to Cast Deceased Wife’s Absentee Ballot in 2024 Election
body: Press Release Tijeras Man Indicted for Attempting to Cast Deceased Wife’s Absentee Ballot in 2024 Election Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A resident of Tijeras, New Mexico, has been indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of fraudulent voting. According to court documents, in October 2024, Patrick H. Perea , 62, attempted to cast his deceased wife’s absentee ballot in the November 2024 general election by submitting it to the Bureau of Elections of the Bernalillo County Clerk’s Office in Albuquerque. If convicted, Perea faces up to five years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000. “Dead people can’t vote” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison said. “Casting a ballot that belongs to someone else is a deliberate abuse of our election process and a federal crime. Election integrity depends on protecting the process from fraud and ensuring that unlawful votes do not dilute the votes of legitimate voters. If you try to vote for another person, you will be caught and we will prosecute.” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case. Federal prosecutors commended the Bernalillo County Clerk’s Office Bureau of Elections for its critical role in intercepting the ballot before it could be counted and assisting this investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sean J. Sullivan and Emil J. Kiehne are prosecuting the case. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-283

title: Methamphetamine trafficker who led law enforcement on a high-speed pursuit sentenced to 230 months in federal prison
body: Press Release Methamphetamine trafficker who led law enforcement on a high-speed pursuit sentenced to 230 months in federal prison Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas LUBBOCK, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a New Mexico man who was caught with over 300 grams of methamphetamine and a loaded Glock pistol after leading multiple West Texas law enforcement agencies on a lengthy high-speed chase was sentenced to just over 19 years in federal prison on Oct. 8. Erik Louis Almaguer, 32, was indicted in February and pleaded guilty in May to possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix imposed a 170‑month sentence for the drug offense, followed by a consecutive 60‑month sentence for the firearm offense, for a total of 230 months. “This defendant put countless motorists and officers at risk in an effort to avoid accountability,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This sentence reflects both the seriousness of his conduct and the strength of the partnerships that make West Texas safer. Because of the swift coordination among our federal, state and local law enforcement partners, a dangerous trafficker was stopped, and significant quantities of methamphetamine and a loaded firearm were removed from our communities.” “Drug traffickers who put innocent lives at risk by fleeing from law enforcement demonstrate a reckless disregard for the safety of our communities,” said DEA Dallas Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “This defendant chose to endanger the public rather than face the consequences of his criminal activity.  Thanks to the coordinated efforts of our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, he will now be held accountable for his actions.” According to court documents, on Oct. 9, 2025, narcotics agents in Lubbock were surveilling Erik Almaguer under suspicion that he was engaged in drug trafficking. A Lubbock Police Department patrol unit attempted to stop his vehicle after he committed a traffic violation, but Almaguer immediately accelerated his vehicle and led officers on a high-speed chase. Almaguer left the Lubbock city limits, traveling towards Brownfield. Multiple law enforcement agencies were called in to assist in stopping Almaguer. The defendant evaded law enforcement all the way from Lubbock to Brownfield, at times traveling over 100 miles per hour. When Almaguer reached Brownfield, officers successfully flattened two of Almaguer’s tires using spike strips. However, he continued to evade, forcing officers to use their patrol units to disable his vehicle. Almaguer exited his vehicle and attempted to flee on foot but was quickly captured. Officers located a torn plastic baggie containing suspected methamphetamine near where Almaguer was taken into custody. Officers searched his vehicle and located over 300 grams of suspected methamphetamine and more than 12 grams of suspected fentanyl powder. A loaded Glock 17 pistol with an extended magazine was found between the driver’s seat and center console. Officers also located a baggie of suspected fentanyl pills in Almaguer’s sock. In plea papers, Almaguer admitted to possessing over 300 grams of methamphetamine with the intent to distribute it to others. He also admitted to possessing a loaded Glock pistol in relation to his drug trafficking. The Drug Enforcement Administration, Lubbock Police Department, Lubbock County Sheriff’s Office, Hockley County Sheriff’s Office, Terry County Sheriff’s Office, and Brownfield Police Department conducted the investigation. Federal, state, and local law enforcement partners collaborated on this investigation under the Caprock Texas High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) initiative. Assistant U.S. Attorney Sean Long from the Lubbock Division prosecuted the case. ### Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Components Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Minnesota Man Sentenced to More Than 8 Years for Travelling to Engage in Sex With a Minor
body: Press Release Minnesota Man Sentenced to More Than 8 Years for Travelling to Engage in Sex With a Minor Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Wisconsin Creighton Mithaugen also has prior conviction for sex with a minor MADISON, WIS. – Chadwick M. Elgersma, United States Attorney for the Western District of Wisconsin, announced that Creighton Mithaugen, 38, Faribault, Minnesota, was sentenced this week by U.S. District Judge William M. Conley to 97 months in federal prison for traveling from Minnesota to Wisconsin to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a minor. The prison term will be followed by a lifetime of supervised release. Mithaugen pleaded guilty to this charge on July 13, 2026. From April 2024 through February 2026, Mithaugen chatted with what he believed to be a 14 or 15-year-old girl, when in reality he was chatting with an undercover law enforcement agent. On February 13, 2026, Mithaugen was arrested after he drove from his residence in Minnesota to a prearranged meeting spot in Rhinelander, Wisconsin, to meet the purposed minor to engage in sexual activity. At the sentencing hearing, Judge Conley considered Mithaugen’s history, which included a conviction for sex with a fifteen-year-old girl in 2007 and credible allegations he touched a ten-year-old girl in 2022, and concluded that Mithaugen was a repeat and dangerous sex offender. Judge Conley found that a lengthy sentence was necessary to protect some of the most vulnerable members of society from Mithaugen’s predatory behavior. The charge against Mithaugen was the result of an investigation conducted by the Oneida County Sheriff’s Office, the Rhinelander Police Department, the Wisconsin Department of Justice Division of Criminal Investigation, and the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Assistant U.S. Attorney Julie Pfluger prosecuted this case. This investigation was a part of Project Safe Childhood (PSC), a nationwide initiative to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Wisconsin, Western

title: New York cocaine trafficker sentenced to six years in prison

title: Alien Illegally and Unlawfully in the U.S. Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Distribution of Cocaine and Firearm Offenses
body: Press Release Alien Illegally and Unlawfully in the U.S. Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Distribution of Cocaine and Firearm Offenses Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Kentucky Louisville, KY – A Mexican national illegally and unlawfully living in Louisville was sentenced on October 7, 2026, to 10 years in prison for distribution of cocaine, possession of a firearm by an alien illegally and unlawfully in the United States, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. U.S. Attorney Kyle Bumgarner of the Western District of Kentucky, acting Deputy Special Agent in Charge Michael Perez of Homeland Security Investigations Nashville, Special Agent in Charge Jim Scott of the DEA Louisville Field Division, and Chief Paul L. Humphrey of the Louisville Metro Police Department made the announcement. Gabriel Aguilar-Benitez, 36, a citizen of Mexico, unlawfully living in Louisville, Kentucky, was sentenced to 10 years in prison, followed by 4 years of supervised release, for distribution of cocaine, possession of a firearm by an alien illegally and unlawfully in the United States, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. On five different occasions between February 10, 2025, and April 17, 2025, Aguilar-Benitez sold cocaine to a confidential source. On April 22, 2025, a federal search warrant was executed at Aguilar-Benitez’s residence at 8015 Daffodil Drive, Louisville, Kentucky, and on Aguilar-Benitez’s 2009 Chevrolet Tahoe. 75.84 grams of cocaine, a Kimber .45 caliber pistol, a Lorcin .380 caliber pistol, and ammunition were found and seized. The total amount of cocaine in the case is 537.29 grams. The Kimber .45 caliber pistol and the Lorcin .380 caliber pistol were possessed by Aguilar-Benitez while he was an alien illegally and unlawfully in the United States and in furtherance of the drug trafficking crime. United States Attorney Kyle Bumgarner stated, “Aguilar-Benitez is illegally in this country selling substantial amounts of cocaine while armed. He is a danger to the citizens of Louisville. Fortunately, he will spend the next 10 years in federal prison and be deported back to Mexico.” “HSI is committed to working with our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to eliminate crime and dangerous drugs from our communities,” said HSI Nashville acting Deputy Special Agent in Charge Michael Perez. “This sentence reflects that commitment and holds the defendant accountable for his actions.” LMPD Chief Paul L. Humphrey stated, "Drugs and illegal guns are a dangerous combination that puts lives at risk. This case is another example of the important work being done by local and federal law enforcement to get dangerous criminals off our streets and make Louisville safer.” There is no parole in the federal system. The case was investigated by HSI Nashville, the Louisville Metro Police Department, and the DEA Louisville Field Division. Assistant U.S. Attorney Erwin Roberts prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. ### Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Operation Take Back America Component USAO - Kentucky, Western

title: Two Dominican Republic Nationals Extradited to Face Cyberstalking and Sextortion Conspiracy Charges in Puerto Rico
body: Press Release Two Dominican Republic Nationals Extradited to Face Cyberstalking and Sextortion Conspiracy Charges in Puerto Rico Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – Dominican authorities extradited Patricia Joanna Almonte-Frías and her partner Rineldys Feliciano Díaz-Cuevas to the United States to face cyberstalking and sextortion conspiracy charges filed in the District of Puerto Rico, announced Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. The defendants were arrested in the Dominican Republic on August 19, 2026, at the request of the United States, and extradited to Puerto Rico on September 30, 2026. According to court documents, Patricia Joanna Almonte-Frías and Rineldys Feliciano Díaz-Cuevas operated an international, financially motivated “sextortion” scheme that conspired to engage in, and did engage in, cyberstalking and intestate threats. The defendants, operating from the Dominican Republic, identified and sextorted victims using Facebook, WhatsApp, and other social media platforms. Almonte-Frías used her image to encourage victims in Puerto Rico to share online sexually explicit photos and videos (which were secretly recorded). Subsequently, defendant Díaz-Cuevas and other co-conspirators then extorted victims to send money under threat of exposing the compromising images to the victims’ family and friends. In some instances, the defendants created photo collages by combining the victim’s sexually explicit images with images of minors, thereby giving the false impression that victims were involved in sexual relationships with minors. On multiple occasions, the victims paid the demanded amounts, emptied their accounts, and the defendants still carried out the threats and distributed the victims’ sexual images to the victims’ online network of friends and family members. “These defendants ran a calculated scheme that preyed on trust, fear, and vulnerability, leaving lasting harm in its wake,” said Héctor Ramírez‑Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. “Sextortion is a ruthless crime, and today’s prosecution makes clear that those who exploit victims—no matter where they hide—will be identified, pursued, and held to account.” “In today’s ever-changing digital environment, criminals will develop creative ways to target victims and exploit them. Extortion is a serious crime that can cause lasting financial and psychological harm to its victims,” said Carlos R. Goris, Special Agent in Charge of FBI San Juan. “The FBI encourages all citizens to remain vigilant online and report to the authorities if you suspect you have been a victim of extortion. Your report will help law enforcement disrupt these networks and prevent others from becoming victims. The FBI demonstrates once again that no matter where you are, we will find you and bring you to justice.” Almonte-Frías and Díaz-Cuevas are charged with conspiracy to cyberstalk and send interstate threats in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371. The defendants made their initial court appearances on October 1, 2026 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Marcos E. López of the U.S. District Court for the District of Puerto Rico. If convicted, they face a maximum penalty of five years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. The FBI in San Juan, Puerto Rico investigated the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, FBI Legal Attaché in Santo Domingo, the U.S. Marshals Service, and law enforcement partners in the Dominican Republic provided substantial assistance in securing the arrest and extradition to the United States of Almonte-Frías and Díaz-Cuevas. Assistant U.S. Attorney Julián Radzinschi, of the Financial Fraud and Public Corruption Division, is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. ### Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Cybercrime Financial Fraud Components Criminal - Office of International Affairs Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico Press Release Number: 2026-108

The defendants were arrested in the Dominican Republic on August 19, 2026, at the request of the United States, and extradited to Puerto Rico on September 30, 2026.

title: Medical Supply Company Owner Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison for $30M Medicare, TRICARE, and CHAMPVA Fraud
body: Press Release Medical Supply Company Owner Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison for $30M Medicare, TRICARE, and CHAMPVA Fraud Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs An Oklahoma business owner and chiropractor was sentenced yesterday to 14 years in prison for his role in a years-long scheme that attempted to bilk Medicare, TRICARE, and the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) out of over $30 million for orthotics braces, continuous glucose monitors, and other durable medical equipment (DME) that beneficiaries did not want or need. “Yesterday's 14-year sentence shows that health care fraud does not pay,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Department of Justice's National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The Department is committed to bringing to justice those who corrupt our health care system by paying illegal kickbacks, submitting false claims, deceiving programs that serve our seniors, service members, and veterans, and treating sensitive patient information like a commodity to be bought and sold.” “Fraud against federal health care programs is a direct attack on the public’s trust and on the vulnerable individuals these programs are meant to protect, and the jury’s verdict and sentencing of Mark Loftis demonstrate that schemes of this kind will be met with decisive action and significant consequences,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General. “HHS-OIG will not hesitate to investigate and dismantle criminal conduct wherever it threatens the integrity of federal programs, and this case reflects the unwavering commitment of our agency and our law-enforcement partners to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure that those who defraud the government are held fully accountable.” “Healthcare fraud drains millions of dollars from federally funded programs, and we all pay the price,” said Special Agent in Charge Rodney Crawford of the FBI Tampa Field Office. “Today’s sentence underscores the FBI’s steadfast commitment to aggressively pursuing those who engage in kickback schemes and other fraudulent practices.” “As the law enforcement arm of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) is committed to safeguarding the integrity of the TRICARE program,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Nakia M. Alexander of the DCIS Southeast Field Office. “This investigation is an example of a healthcare fraud scheme that directly affected American service members and their families. I applaud the collaborative work of the investigative agencies and the Department of Justice that led to today’s sentencing.” “Fraud schemes targeting VA programs and services compromise their integrity and divert funds from veterans who rely on these benefits,” said Inspector General Cheryl L. Mason, Department of Veterans Affairs. “The VA OIG works every day with our law enforcement partners to identify fraudsters and hold them accountable.” According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Dr. Mark Loftis, 39, of Cushing, Oklahoma, and his co-conspirators did not disclose to Medicare the ownership and management of the DME company Back Pain Home Supplies LLC dba EZ Medical Supply. Loftis and his co-conspirators hid from Medicare that unenrolled entities were billing claims through the DME company. Lofits paid over a million dollars in illegal kickbacks, including through a shell marketing company, to marketers, purported telemedicine companies, and a call center that persuaded elderly and disabled Americans to disclose their personal information and receive DME they did not need. Loftis and his co-conspirators also purchased sham doctors’ orders for orthotic braces, continuous glucose monitors, and DME that were generated by telemedicine doctors and nurse practitioners who never examined, and often never spoke to, the beneficiaries. Loftis and his co-conspirators submitted over $30 million in false and fraudulent claims and were paid over $8 million. Loftis and his co-conspirators frequently billed for multiple orthotic braces at a time, including in one example eight braces for a single beneficiary. After a 12-day jury trial ending in July 2026, Loftis was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud. In addition to the prison sentence, Loftis was ordered to pay over $8 million in restitution and to forfeit over $560,000. HHS-OIG, FBI, DCIS, and VA-OIG investigated the case. Assistant Deputy Chief Catherine Wagner and Trial Attorney Raymond Beckering III of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1159

title: Jacksonville Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Jacksonville Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Distribution, Receipt, and Possession of Child Pornography Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of Illinois SPRINGFIELD, Ill. – A Jacksonville, Illinois, man, Daniel Brannan, 48, was sentenced last week to 12 years in prison, to be followed by a 10-year term of supervised release, for distribution, receipt, and possession of child pornography. At the sentencing hearing on September 29, 2026, the government established that Brannan had engaged in the distribution and trading of multiple videos of child pornography between April and May 2025 on an online chatting application. These videos included prepubescent minors engaged in sex acts with adults. Also at the hearing, U.S. District Judge Colleen R. Lawless described the number of files possessed, over five thousand images and thirty-four videos; found that Brannan had engaged in trading in child pornography; and stated that images that he possessed included toddlers and infants, as well as bondage and humiliation. In June 2026, Brannan pleaded guilty to distribution of child pornography, receipt of child pornography, and possession of child pornography. Brannan remains in the custody of the United States Marshals Service where he has been since his arrest in December 2025. The statutory penalties for distribution and receipt of child pornography are not less than five years and up to 20 years’ imprisonment, up to a life term of supervised release, up to a $250,000 fine, and restitution. The statutory penalties for possession of child pornography are not more than 10 years’ imprisonment, five years to a life term of supervised release, and up to a $250,000 fine. The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Springfield Field Office, and the Illinois Attorney General’s Office investigated the case with assistance from the Jacksonville, Illinois, Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Tanner K. Jacobs represented the government in the prosecution. The case against Brannan was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative by the Department of Justice to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov. title: Leader of Global Violent Extremist Network ‘764’ Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Sexually Exploit Minors
body: Press Release Leader of Global Violent Extremist Network ‘764’ Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Sexually Exploit Minors Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Prasan Nepal, 21, also known by the online moniker “Trippy,” of High Point, North Carolina, pleaded guilty yesterday to conspiracy to commit sexual exploitation of a child. “This is the latest victory in the FBI’s work with partners to dismantle the violent 764 network,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Prasan Nepal, a leader of 764, pleaded guilty for his role in exploiting juveniles - not only breaking the law himself but recruiting others to participate in the heinous conduct targeting kids online through sexual assault, pornography, animal crushing, and more. Dismantling 764 and their online network has been a top priority for this FBI, with a nearly 500% increase in 764 related arrests last year with our state and local partners. We are finding these criminal actors all over the country no matter where they operate. Let there be no doubt that the FBI and our partners will use all our resources to protect children and bring to justice those who commit acts of terrible abuse. “ “Nepal used his leadership role within 764 to orchestrate the systematic exploitation, torture, and psychological destruction of children for the twisted satisfaction of an online network built on cruelty and chaos,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “He directed unspeakable crimes and then treated the suffering of the group’s victims as currency to be traded among his co-conspirators. We will not rest until every member of this network, and others like it, are held accountable.” “This case exposes a world where cruelty is currency, violence is entertainment, and children are treated as targets in a game of domination and control,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia. “What Nepal and his co‑conspirators built was not just a criminal operation, it was a deliberate campaign to corrupt the vulnerable and dismantle the guardrails of civilized society. Yesterday’s plea is a victory for every child they sought to harm, and a warning to anyone who believes they can hide behind an encrypted screen: we will find you, and we will stop you.” Nepal operated as a senior leader within “764,” a nihilistic violent extremist network that, according to court documents, engaged in a wide range of criminal conduct across the United States and abroad — including coordinated efforts to exploit minors, extort vulnerable victims, and inflict psychological harm as part of an organized ideology promoting chaos and societal destabilization. According to court documents, Nepal and co‑defendant Leonidas Varagiannis, known as “War,” served as core leaders of 764 and its inner subgroup, 764 Inferno. From approximately 2021 through 2025, Nepal and others used encrypted platforms to coordinate the exploitation of minors worldwide. They directed members, enforced “rules,” managed recruitment, and oversaw the production and circulation of materials used to manipulate and coerce victims. Membership in 764 required prospective recruits to produce “content” that furthered the group’s extremist and abusive aims. Individuals who complied gained status; those who did not were excluded. Nepal and Varagiannis maintained strict control over membership, monitored activity, and issued instructions designed to expand the network’s reach and increase the volume of exploitative material. Court documents detail the involvement of co‑conspirators operating inside the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. One D.C.-based individual allegedly stored network material on digital devices within the District and participated in conduct aimed at coercing minor victims. Other U.S.-based co‑conspirators engaged in coordinated online extortion schemes that targeted minors in multiple states and foreign jurisdictions. The stored content included images of the words “764 Kills” written in red on a wall and a video of 15-year-old minor victim standing topless with her breasts exposed, talking to someone on a live chat while she poured bleach on her arm and set her arm on fire. Federal investigators have identified more than a dozen active co‑conspirators associated with Nepal and Varagiannis, many of whom operated under aliases and interacted regularly in encrypted group channels. Their activities reflected an organized, hierarchical structure designed to recruit vulnerable victims, generate exploitative material, and cultivate notoriety within the network. 764 and 764 Inferno were built on a shared extremist ideology that embraced social collapse and celebrated violence. Members used encrypted applications to: Identify vulnerable minors online, Manipulate victims into compliance, Coerce individuals using threats and intimidation, Distribute extremist and exploitative content, and Promote members based on the severity of material they helped generate. The defendants and their co-conspirators around the world used the Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other gore and violent material to create digital “Lorebooks,” which were used as digital currency within the 764 network, traded, archived in encrypted “vaults,” and used as a means to recruit new members or maintain status within the network. The defendants instructed other members in grooming tactics and set content production expectations for new recruits. In multiple instances, defendants threatened and caused their victims to engage in self-mutilation, online and in-person sexual acts, harm to animals, sexual exploitation of siblings and others, acts of violence, threats of violence, suicide, and murder. A guide instructing members on “grooming” victims into producing content for 764 and advised members to target particularly vulnerable victims, such as individuals with depression or mental illness. According to court documents, the defendants exploited at least eight minor victims across multiple jurisdictions, with some content traced back to children as young as 13 years-old. The network’s activities spanned from late 2020 through early 2025. The guide also provided instructions on “Extortion,” and advised prospective 764 members to manipulate girls and to groom them into providing personal information that could then be used to force them to create “blood content.” Nepal joined 764 in or around early 2021, and worked with others known and unknown, including Individual 1, to establish the group. After Individual 1’s arrest on or about Aug. 25, 2021, Nepal emerged as a leader of 764 and remained in that position through April 2025. In his capacity as a member and leader of 764, Nepal used several online monikers, including, “Leather Jacket,” “Rebirth,” “Indras Jester,” and “KingKrampus,” but he was most widely known in 764 Inferno as “Trippy.” Nepal was arrested in 2025 and charged alongside Varagiannis as part of a sweeping international investigation involving the District of Columbia, federal field offices across the United States, and law enforcement authorities abroad. Yesterday’s plea represents one of the most significant developments yet in dismantling 764’s leadership structure. Variagiannis is currently being held at Grevena Prison in northern Greece and is expected to have a trial in the next six months on charges related to child pornography and participation in a criminal organization. Nepal faces a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison. Sentencing is set for March 5, 2027. This case is being investigated by the FBI Washington Field Office with significant assistance from the FBI New York Field Office, FBI Charlotte Field Office, and international partners. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of North Carolina also provided invaluable assistance. The case is being prosecuted by Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Karen Shinskie and Janani Iyengar for the District of Columbia. The Justice Department remains vigilant against the threat of NVE networks like 764 that operate within the United States and around the globe. NVEs often target vulnerable individuals, including minors, using social media platforms to share CSAM and gore material, and groom victims toward committing acts of violence. Victims are often extorted, coerced, compelled, and blackmailed into complying with NVE demands, including self-mutilation, online and in-person sexual acts, harm to animals, sexual exploitation of siblings and others, acts of violence, threats of violence, suicide, and murder. For more information on how to protect children and others, read about the online risks here: https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/parents-and-caregivers-protecting-your-kids and the FBI’s March 2025 public service announcement. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice.  Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 99 Border-Related Cases This Week
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 99 Border-Related Cases This Week Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California SAN DIEGO – Federal prosecutors in the Southern District of California filed 99 border-related cases this week, including charges of bringing in aliens for financial gain, reentering the U.S. after deportation, and importation of controlled substances. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California is the fourth-busiest federal district, largely due to a high volume of border-related crimes. This district, encompassing San Diego and Imperial counties, shares a 140-mile border with Mexico. It includes the San Ysidro Port of Entry, the world’s busiest land border crossing, connecting San Diego (America’s eighth largest city) and Tijuana (Mexico’s second largest city). In addition to reactive border-related crimes, the Southern District of California also prosecutes a significant number of proactive cases related to terrorism, organized crime, drugs, white-collar fraud, violent crime, cybercrime, human trafficking and national security. Recent developments in those and other significant areas of prosecution can be found here . A sample of border-related arrests this week: On October 3, 2026, Efrain Antonio Avalos, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Transportation of Illegal Aliens. According to a complaint, Border Patrol Agents attempted to conduct a vehicle stop on a Hyundai suspected of transporting illegal aliens.  Defendant failed to yield and instead sped up to about 105 miles per hour. Border Patrol Agents deployed a vehicle immobilization device and the vehicle’s left tires made positive contact with the device. Defendant continued to flee at a high rate of speed, failed to stop at a stop sign and collided into an oncoming vehicle. The Defendant exited the vehicle after the collision Border Patrol Agents observed the material witness crawling away from the Hyundai with carpet coverings on his feet and his head covered in blood. The Hyundai then caught on fire. On October 5, 2026, Victor Hugo Gutierrez De La Torre, a Mexican citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered 1,038 pounds of methamphetamine concealed in the fuel tank of the 2020 Volvo VNL 760 tractor the defendant was driving as he applied for entry to the U.S. at the Otay Mesa Port of Entry. September 6, 2026, Justin Jimenez, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered 91 pounds of Xanax concealed in the floorboards of his Volkswagen Jetta GLI the defendant was driving as he applied for entry to the U.S. at the San Ysidro Port of Entry. The immigration cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE ERO), Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), with the support and assistance of state and local law enforcement partners. Indictments and criminal complaints are merely allegations, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Jury Convicts Lake City Woman in $2.9 Million Fraud Case
body: Press Release Jury Convicts Lake City Woman in $2.9 Million Fraud Case Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Jacksonville, Florida – A federal jury has found Treashonna P. Graham (42, Lake City) guilty of all charges in a 13-count indictment, including conspiracy to commit wire fraud and multiple counts of wire fraud and money laundering. Graham faces up to 20 years in prison for the conspiracy and each wire fraud offense and up to 10 years’ imprisonment for each money laundering offense. Graham will be sentenced on January 19, 2027. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court records, Graham and her conspirator/co-defendant, Joey Williams, created a company called “Grant Bae,” which purportedly assisted minority business owners to obtain government grants. Graham charged a fee for her services and advised clients that the company was in the process of obtaining grant money on their behalf. The evidence at trial proved that Graham never hired companies to help locate or obtain grants nor did she help to write any grant applications for her clients. More than 1,000 individuals were victimized by her fraudulent scheme. In total, Graham stole approximately $2,.9 million and used those funds to live an extravagant lifestyle. Graham used the fraudulent proceeds to purchase vehicles, jewelry, clothing, and other personal property. She also gambled away hundreds of thousands of dollars at local casinos. Williams previously pleaded guilty for his role in this case and is pending sentencing. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney John Cannizzaro. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Previously Removed Illegal Alien Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison for Methamphetamine Trafficking and Ammunition Offense
body: Press Release Previously Removed Illegal Alien Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison for Methamphetamine Trafficking and Ammunition Offense Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California SANTA ANA – A previously removed illegal alien was sentenced to 120 months in federal prison for possessing with intent to distribute methamphetamine, unlawfully possessing ammunition as a felon, and illegally reentering the United States after prior deportations. The case was investigated as part of Operation Guardian Angel, an initiative targeting violent offenders, narcotics trafficking, and previously removed criminal aliens operating in local communities. Juan Jose Guerra‑Renteria, 46, a Mexican national who had been deported in 2006 and again in 2020, was sentenced on October 8, 2026, for possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, being a felon in possession of ammunition, and illegal reentry. United States District Judge Monica Ramirez Almadani sentenced him to 120 months’ imprisonment on the drug trafficking and firearms counts and 29 months on the illegal reentry count, to be served concurrently. “Thanks to Operation Guardian Angel, criminal illegal aliens like Guerra‑Renteria are being identified and removed from our communities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “This sentence reflects the seriousness of defendant’s conduct and his repeated disregard for federal law. My office will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to safeguard our communities and ensure that dangerous criminal illegal aliens are held accountable with federal prison time.” According to the plea agreement, on October 14, 2025, law enforcement conducted a traffic stop on Guerra‑Renteria in Orange County, during which officers located over 211.9 grams of methamphetamine and 56 rounds of .45‑caliber ammunition. At the time he possessed the ammunition, Guerra‑Renteria had multiple prior felony convictions, making it illegal for him to possess ammunition under federal law. Following his 2020 removal, he knowingly and voluntarily reentered the United States without authorization from the Attorney General or the Department of Homeland Security. This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Orange Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Kevin Y. Fu of the Orange County Office prosecuted the case. title: Local man sentenced to 33 months in federal prison for threatening the President and federal law enforcement officers
body: Press Release Local man sentenced to 33 months in federal prison for threatening the President and federal law enforcement officers Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a Springtown, Texas, man who repeatedly issued violent threats against the President of the United States and federal immigration officers was sentenced to 33 months in federal prison. On June 9, 2025, Francisco Jesus Mena, 37, pleaded guilty to one count of threatening a federal official. U.S. Chief District Judge Reed O’Connor imposed the sentence today. “Threats against the President and federal officers are crimes that my office takes very seriously,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “We will continue to prosecute individuals like the defendant who seek to intimidate, impede or retaliate against federal law enforcement for performing vital national security and immigration related duties.” “This sentence makes clear that conveying violent online threats is a serious criminal offense with substantial consequences, said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI remains committed to ensuring that individuals who exploit digital platforms to intimidate, coerce, or instill fear are held accountable.” “The U.S. Secret Service investigates all threats against our protectees,” said Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Secret Service Dallas Field Office Christina Foley. “Threats against the President will not be tolerated. We continue to work alongside our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to investigate these threats and will hold those who threaten to harm any of our protectees accountable.” According to court documents, between May 13 and May 25, 2025, Mena made numerous threats against President Trump and ICE agents in a series of online messages posted to social media. The defendant repeatedly threatened to assault and murder the President, writing variations of “KILL TRUMP” across multiple dates and platforms. He also issued threats directed at federal law enforcement officers stating that if ICE agents came to his residence, he would “respond with a gunfight,” and claiming he had previously stabbed an ICE agent and “would love to do this again.” On several occasions, Mena claimed that ICE personnel would be targeted next and encouraged violence against federal officers and white people, stating that individuals with “blue eyes and white skin will get chopped,” and offering payment or solicitation to harm the President. He further stated he did not need money to “take out Trump” and requested access to a sniper. The FBI and the U.S. Secret Service conducted the investigation with assistance from local law enforcement. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justin Beck and Ethan Womble from the Fort Worth Division prosecuted the case. ### Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topic National Security Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Shooting on the Grounds of Watkins Elementary School Yields 32 Years in Prison for D.C. Man
body: Press Release Shooting on the Grounds of Watkins Elementary School Yields 32 Years in Prison for D.C. Man Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Antonio Hawley, 23, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today in D.C. Superior Court for the October 2021 shooting death of 26-year-old Aaron Wiggins on the sports field of Watkins Elementary School, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “A flag football rivalry ended in murder. Antonio Hawley fired 17 shots at Aaron Wiggins and killed him,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “No family should have to endure the pain of losing a loved one to senseless violence. Today’s sentence cannot undo that loss, but it sends a clear message: if you take a life through violence, you will face serious consequences.” Hawley was found guilty on February 3, 2026, of one count of first-degree murder while armed, one count of possession of a firearm during a crime of violence, and one count of carrying a pistol without a license. Hawley was 18 years old at the time of the shooting. The Honorable Judge Danya Dayson ordered him to 32 years of incarceration to be followed by five years of supervised release. According to the government’s evidence, at approximately 9:45 p.m. on October 6, 2021, Hawley and Wiggins were playing against each other in a flag football scrimmage on the sports field of Watkins Elementary School when the field lights cut off. The two teams decided to finish one last play, and Wiggins caught the winning touchdown, ending the game. Throughout the game, there was continued trash talk between Wiggins and members of Hawley’s team, intensifying after that final play. When members of both flag football teams started to gather their belongings to leave the field, Hawley retrieved a handgun from a teammate’s bag and approached Wiggins, firing at him 17 times and hitting the victim 13 times. Wiggins died at the scene. Joining in the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. In announcing the sentence, U.S. Attorney Pirro and Interim Chief Carroll commended the work of those who investigated the case from the Metropolitan Police Department. They also acknowledged Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jin Park and Mark Levy, who prosecuted the case. 2021 CF1 007260 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Tallahassee Man Sentenced to Over 20 Years for  Distribution of Methamphetamine and Cocaine
body: Press Release Tallahassee Man Sentenced to Over 20 Years for  Distribution of Methamphetamine and Cocaine Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Tedrick Childs, 46, of Tallahassee, Florida, has been sentenced to 21 years and six months in federal prison after pleading guilty to one count of distribution of cocaine and one count of distribution of methamphetamine. Childs, who was on supervised release for a 2018 federal drug conviction, was also sentenced to 33 months in federal prison for violating the terms of his supervised release. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the sentence. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This repeat offender’s continued criminality after a prior federal conviction clearly demonstrated that the only way we can protect our community is by keeping him locked away behind federal bars. Thanks to the aggressive prosecution by my office, we have ensured his days of running drugs on our streets are over.” Court records indicate that the defendant was identified by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) as a poly-drug trafficker in the Tallahassee area. During an undercover operation, DEA  purchased cocaine and methamphetamine from the defendant between November and December 2025. In 2017, Childs was convicted in federal court for distribution of cocaine, and he was serving a term of supervised release as part of his sentence in that case when he sold drugs in 2025. “Being on supervised release gives people returning to civilian life the opportunity to make better life choices,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Trafficking in cocaine and methamphetamine is not helping the communities and not the correct choice.” The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. body: Press Release Gainesville Man Pleads Guilty to Convenience Store Robbery Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Denzel Dyshaun Flagg, 27, of Gainesville, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of Hobbs Act Robbery. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution was made possible by the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners, who tracked down this defendant so we could hold him accountable for his role in this violent crime. We owe it to our citizens to protect them from the predations of violent criminals and to seek maximum punishment to hold those offenders accountable and deter future crime.” Court documents reflect that on February 18, 2025, the defendant participated in the robbery of the Eastside Food Store in Gainesville, Florida. During the robbery, two other individuals entered the store wearing ski masks, and one of them pointed a gun directly at the face of the store clerk before stealing cash from the register. The defendant acted as the getaway driver. Flagg faces a maximum sentence of twenty years’ imprisonment. Sentencing is scheduled for November 3, 2026, at the United States Courthouse in Gainesville before United States Chief District Judge Allen C. Winsor. The case involved a joint investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Alachua County Sherriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Adam Hapner and James McCain. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . title: Two Women Charged with Helping Violent Inmates Escape from DeKalb County Jail
body: Press Release Two Women Charged with Helping Violent Inmates Escape from DeKalb County Jail Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA — A federal grand jury indicted Melayna Whatley and Gabriela Ortis for allegedly helping three inmates, including a federal prisoner serving a life sentence, escape from the DeKalb County Jail in December 2025. “Every jailbreak puts the public at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “Thankfully, quick action by numerous law enforcement agencies ensured the lightning-fast capture of the men who escaped from DeKalb County late last year. Now, the women who allegedly helped them bust free must face the consequences for unleashing terror into our community.” “This was far more than an escape from jail—it put an innocent member of the public directly in harm’s way,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “These defendants allegedly helped violent fugitives evade capture, and their actions contributed to a dangerous chain of events that ended with an innocent woman being kidnapped and held against her will. The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to hold accountable anyone who assists violent offenders and puts our communities at risk.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the indictment, and other information presented in court: In June 2025, Stevenson Charles was sentenced in the Southern District of Florida to life in prison for carjacking, kidnapping, bank robbery, and brandishing a firearm. On December 5, 2025, the U.S. Marshals Service transferred him to the DeKalb County Jail in Decatur, Georgia, to face additional state charges. On December 21, 2025, Charles and fellow inmates Yusuf Minor and Noad Yohannes, acting in concert, escaped from the DeKalb County Jail and fled to Florida with the alleged assistance of Melayna Whatley and Gabriela Ortis. Whatley allegedly served as the outside conduit for the escape by making phone calls and text messages on Minor’s behalf to locate a getaway driver before the escape. On the night of the escape, Whatley allegedly allowed Charles, Minor, and Yohannes to use her Flat Shoals Road residence to temporarily evade capture and to use her cellular telephone to contact additional co-conspirators. Gabriela Ortis allegedly arranged the escapees’ transportation on the night of the escape by hiring them a Lyft rideshare driver. After the escapees entered the Lyft vehicle, Charles, Minor, and Yohannes allegedly put an item around the driver’s neck, dragged her into the backseat, tied her hands together, threatened her, and drove her vehicle nearly 700 miles to Broward County, Florida with her inside. Law enforcement captured the escapees and rescued the Lyft driver on December 22, 2025. On February 27, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Lauderdale found Charles guilty of conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, Hobbs Act robbery, and possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. On March 27, 2026, Minor pled guilty to conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, and Hobbs Act robbery. On May 5, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Lauderdale found Yohannes guilty of the same three crimes. On September 23, 2026, a federal grand jury in Atlanta indicted Melayna Whatley, 30, of DeKalb County, Georgia, and Gabriela Ortis, 22, of Miami, Florida, on charges of conspiracy to aid and assist escape, aiding and assisting an escape, and harboring and concealing an escaped prisoner. Law enforcement arrested Whatley on September 29, 2026, and Ortis appeared in federal court yesterday following her arrest. Members of the public are reminded that the indictment only contains charges. The defendants are presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with valuable assistance provided by the United States Marshals Service and DeKalb County Sheriff’s Office. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . title: Syracuse Man Charged With Receiving Child Pornography
Total of Four Defendants Plead Guilty in Connection with Widespread  Child Exploitation Conspiracy
body: Press Release Total of Four Defendants Plead Guilty in Connection with Widespread  Child Exploitation Conspiracy Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Four defendants have now pled guilty in connection with a multi-jurisdictional child exploitation conspiracy that included the trafficking of child pornography produced during the conspiracy. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone, and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement. The defendants involved in the case are: Devin LaValley, age 38, of Burlington, New York; Melissa McDougal, age 30, of Pulaski, New York; Grace Balthazor, age 34, of Elmira, New York; and Roxanne Clark, age 45, of Bristol, Vermont. As part of their guilty pleas, the defendants admitted to their respective involvement in a years-long child exploitation conspiracy and the trafficking of child pornography produced during the conspiracy. LaValley admitted that, years ago, he began intimate relationships with both Balthazor and McDougal, both of whom had access to children. LaValley admitted to then conspiring with both women to get close to the children in their care for the purpose of sexually abusing the children and creating photos and videos depicting that abuse. McDougal and Balthazor also admitted to conspiring with LaValley to abuse the children for the purpose of creating child pornography. LaValley also admitted that after he created the child pornography with McDougal and Balthazor’s assistance, he then distributed the child sexual abuse material to Clark, another woman with whom LaValley had an intimate relationship. For her part, Clark admitted to receiving the child pornography LaValley, McDougal, and Balthazor had produced as part of online communications with LaValley in which she and LaValley discussed their mutual interest in sexually abusing children. At sentencing, LaValley, McDougal, and Balthazor face a mandatory minimum term of 15 years in federal prison and maximum sentence of 30 years for the conspiracy charge. The receipt and distribution charges to which Clark and LaValley have pled guilty carry a mandatory minimum term of five years in federal prison and maximum terms of 20 years. Each charge carries a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “I commend HSI and the New York State Police for the incredible investigative work that led to these four convictions. I also want to acknowledge the urgency with which HSI and State Police identified and arrested the various defendants, several of whom lived in other districts. The result of their diligent work was the identification and protection of multiple children who likely would have continued to be victimized by the defendants had it not been for the dedicated agents and investigators involved. My office remains steadfast in its commitment to work closely with our federal, state, and local partners to do whatever we can to protect our communities from the threat posed by individuals, like the defendants here, who seek to harm the most vulnerable among us.” Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone said, “Those who exploit children and trade in images of their abuse inflict profound and lasting harm on victims, families, and entire communities. These guilty pleas hold all four defendants accountable for their roles in a calculated, years-long conspiracy that preyed on vulnerable children and perpetuated their victimization through the production and distribution of child sexual abuse material. HSI Syracuse and our law enforcement partners will pursue every available lead to identify predators, disrupt child-exploitation networks and safeguard children in our communities.” NYSP Superintendent James stated, “Child predators will go through extreme lengths to exploit children and conduct the most reprehensible of acts. As we fight for the victims and all those affected, we hope the justice brought forth provides a sense of peace that these individuals will never commit a crime like this again. I thank our State Police members, the United States Attorney’s Office, and the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations for their consistent, proactive work on this case.” HSI and NYSP investigated the case with the assistance of the Office of the Vermont Attorney General. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Adrian S. LaRochelle as a part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Azerbaijani National Pleads Guilty to $1 Million Wire Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme Against the United States Postal Service
body: Press Release Azerbaijani National Pleads Guilty to $1 Million Wire Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme Against the United States Postal Service Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Orlando, Florida – Khayyam Arif Oglu Farajov (40), an Azerbaijani national, has pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and one count of money laundering in connection with a scheme to fraudulently obtain payments from the United States Postal Service (USPS). Farajov faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison on each count. A sentencing date has not yet been set. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to the plea agreement, Farajov owned and operated Talishco LLC, a trucking and freight brokerage company in Orlando. In May 2022, Farajov enrolled Talishco in the USPS “Freight Auction” program to transport bulk mail for the USPS. Between June 2022 and January 2023, Farajov bid on and was awarded hundreds of contracts to transport mail across the country on behalf of the USPS. After being awarded the contracts, Farajov routinely and intentionally did not send trucks to do the work. When USPS staff asked where the trucks were, he made false excuses, such as claiming he had lost contact with his drivers or that they were running behind schedule, which forced the USPS to reassign the work to other carriers. Farajov then went back into the platform and exploited the system by falsely marking the loads as delivered and triggering payment from USPS even though he had not performed the contracted routes. Farajov obtained more than $1 million from this scheme. After he received the funds, he funneled them through a series of bank accounts belonging to shell companies he owned. After reconsolidating the fraud proceeds into two personal investment brokerage accounts, Farajov invested the fraud proceeds in the stock market for his personal enrichment. The United States traced the fraud proceeds and seized the contents of Farajov’s brokerage accounts. Farajov has agreed to forfeit the seized brokerage accounts and pay an additional $993,979 in restitution to the USPS. This case was investigated by the United States Postal Service – Office of Inspector General. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Richard Varadan. The forfeiture is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Nicole Andrejko. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.  Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: First-Time Offender Sentenced to 27 Years in Federal Prison for Attempted Coercion of a Minor
body: Press Release First-Time Offender Sentenced to 27 Years in Federal Prison for Attempted Coercion of a Minor Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – Jonathan Edward Veselka (45, Arizona) was sentenced by U.S. District Judge John L. Badalamenti to 27 years in federal prison, followed by a lifetime term of supervised release, for attempted coercion and enticement of a minor to engage in sexual activity, attempted transportation of a minor with intent to engage in sexual activity, and attempted transfer of obscene material to a minor. Veselka pleaded guilty on June 22, 2026. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, for approximately three weeks, Veselka communicated with an undercover officer, believing it was a 14-year-old girl. Veselka sent the undercover officer sexual photos and videos of himself, asked the undercover explicit sexual questions, and detailed the sexual activity he wished to engage in with the individual he believed to be a 14-year-old girl. Veselka arranged for the purported 14-year-old girl to travel to Las Vegas to engage in sexual activity with him. Veselka had never been arrested prior to this criminal offense. This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Abigail K. King and Courtney Derry. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: Davenport Man Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Davenport Man Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Charges Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Davenport man was sentenced on October 8, 2026, to five years in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a felon. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, Terry Lee Chance, Jr., 33, drove through Davenport in possession of a .40 caliber pistol with an obliterated serial number. Officers with the Davenport Police Department recovered the pistol during a traffic stop of the vehicle Chance drove. After completing his term of imprisonment, Chance will be required to serve a three-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Davenport Police Department investigated the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. Contact MacKenzie Tubbs Public Information Officer 515-473-9300 USAIAS.PAO@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Project Safe Neighborhoods Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Iowa, Southern

title: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads To Conviction of Albany Man For Crack Cocaine Sales
body: Press Release Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads To Conviction of Albany Man For Crack Cocaine Sales Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Kymere Thomas, 28, of Albany, New York, pled guilty before U.S. District Judge Anthony Brindisi on October 5, 2026, to distributing crack cocaine.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. Between March and August 2025, Thomas sold over 50 grams of cocaine, and over 580 grams of crack (cocaine base), in eight separate transactions.  In one of these transactions alone Thomas sold 292 grams of crack, for which he was paid over $11,000.  When officers searched his residence, they found another 650 grams of cocaine and 15 grams of crack.  Thomas was arrested in September 2025 and remained on pre-trial release until his guilty plea, when he was remanded to custody. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “We will aggressively work to dismantle the drug-trafficking networks that threaten the safety of our communities. Our work is far from over, and this guilty plea shows those who choose to spread dangerous narcotics that we are coming for you.  I am grateful to our law enforcement partners for arresting him and that he is finally off our streets.” “By his own admission, Mr. Thomas was responsible for trafficking an enormous amount of cocaine into our communities,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “FBI Albany’s Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) responded with the full weight of its federal, state, and local partnerships, and now Mr. Thomas is heading to federal prison for a least a decade. The FBI is laser-focused on investigating and holding accountable any criminal looking to endanger our communities through the sale of illegal drugs.” Thomas faces a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years, followed by a minimum term of 5 years’ supervised release.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors.  Thomas’s sentencing has been scheduled for January 27, 2027. The FBI investigated the case.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Walter prosecuted the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the FBI, ATF, IRS Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Emergency Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the DEA, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Component USAO - New York, Northern
